title: Plan the repository's executable check fence and declare when harness validation is unavailable
rationale: The factory's independent validation stage only executes commands already recorded in the repository's validation document when the implement stage begins. On a repository whose docs/VALIDATION.md is the generic installed template (no executable commands), validation is silently skipped for the entire run and approval rests solely on the implementer's self-reported evidence and the reviewer's inspection. The planner can see this condition and should plan around it instead of leaving it invisible.
evidence: runs/20261017-200437/events.jsonl:15619 — `validation_skipped, reason: "no commands in docs/VALIDATION.md"`; no `validation-*.log` exists in the run directory while run-state.json records `"review-1": "approve"`. The fence was only created at the document stage (run-state.json results.document), i.e. after validation had already been skipped.
proposed_change: After the paragraph that starts "Choose the smallest validation set proportional to the change's risk", add: "Check whether the repository's validation document (e.g. `docs/VALIDATION.md`) already contains executable, self-terminating check commands; the harness's independent validation stage can only run commands present when implementation begins. If it contains none, say so in the plan and (a) require the implementer to capture, as completion evidence for every acceptance criterion, the exact command plus observed stdout, stderr and exit status, because no independent validation will run this run, and (b) add a step that records those acceptance commands as a fast, self-terminating shell fence in that validation document so the repository gains independent validation from the next run onward. Treat this as validation coverage, not extra instrumentation."

title: Scope blast-radius acceptance criteria to named artefacts, never to 'no existing files'
rationale: A blanket 'no existing files are modified' criterion is treated by later stages as a hard contract, so it silently blocks exactly the documentation work that keeps the repository truthful about the change. The criterion is meant to prevent code and configuration sprawl; as written it also forbids the documentation stage from doing its job.
evidence: runs/20261017-200437/plan.md criterion 4 ("no existing files are modified") and its out-of-scope list. run-state.json results.document: "acceptance criterion 4 ('no existing files are modified') leaves README.md at 0 bytes so the run command is documented only under docs/ — README was not edited to avoid breaking an approved criterion". /Users/iancarroll/dev/hello1/README.md is still empty on main after the merge.
proposed_change: In the paragraph beginning "Clearly label normative requirements", add: "When a criterion limits blast radius, name the artefacts the request concerns ('no existing source, build or configuration file is modified') rather than writing a blanket prohibition on modifying existing files. A blanket rule silently forbids the documentation work that keeps `README.md`, `docs/` and the validation document truthful about the change. If a specific file must remain untouched, name it and give the reason."

title: Record how the test and formatter/linter standards apply while no tooling is committed
rationale: Two clauses of this standard are currently unenforceable in this repository, so every run must re-discover the conflict, document a deviation and leave the standard nominally violated. The documenter explicitly ruled the fix out of its own scope and assigned it to the improvement phase. Recording the scope boundary and its closing condition keeps the rules normative while ending the recurring deviation disclosure.
evidence: review-1.md minor finding on docs/coding-standards.md:4 ('every behaviour change has a test' satisfied only by a documented compromise); run-state.json results.document: "'follow the language's standard formatter and linter' is unenforceable since no formatter, linter, type checker, pyproject.toml or CI config exists, so those checks are genuinely not run"; docs/VALIDATION.md 'Checks not available in this repository' table.
proposed_change: Append a short non-normative section, e.g. '## Current tooling scope', stating: this repository commits no test runner, formatter, linter or type checker and no `pyproject.toml`; until such tooling is committed, (1) the evidence required by 'every behaviour change has a test' is the executable acceptance fence in `docs/VALIDATION.md`, actually executed, with its output captured as completion evidence, and (2) the formatter/linter (and type-checking) clauses apply only to tooling that is configured, and each unconfigured check must be disclosed as not run under `docs/VALIDATION.md` *Blocked Validation*. State that neither rule is relaxed, that this section is removed the day test or lint tooling is committed, and that a behaviour change may then no longer substitute a one-off command for a committed test.

title: Fill the empty README with the run command and document map
rationale: The repository's only entry point is a 0-byte file after the merge, so a reader or agent opening the repo learns nothing about what it does, how to run it or where the governing documents are; the documenter identified this and was blocked from fixing it by an approved acceptance criterion. Adding it here closes the remaining code/doc drift the documenter reported as out of its scope.
evidence: /Users/iancarroll/dev/hello1/README.md is empty (0 bytes) on main after `sf/20261017-200437` was merged (run-state.json `"merge": "merged sf/20261017-200437 into main"`); run-state.json results.document records README was intentionally left untouched, so `python3 hello.py` is documented only inside docs/.
proposed_change: Replace the empty file with a few lines: what the repository is (a single Python 3 script that prints `hello world`), the verified run command `python3 hello.py` (no shebang, so invoke via the interpreter; `python` fallback) with its expected stdout `hello world` and exit status 0, and links to `docs/VALIDATION.md` (executable check set), `docs/architecture.md` (process contract), `docs/coding-standards.md` and `docs/plans/` (per-task plans). Keep it descriptive only; no new normative rules.

title: Make verification commands fail loudly and use shell-portable flags
rationale: Multi-check shell one-liners joined by `&&` suppress later assertions when an early command fails, so an agent can finish a validation command having received no evidence for the checks that never ran, and the surviving output can still look like a pass. GNU-only flags on BSD/macOS hosts (the common agent platform) are a frequent trigger. The implementer self-corrected here only because it noticed the stray error, which is luck rather than a guard.
evidence: runs/20261017-200437/events.jsonl:10783 — tool result `cat: illegal option -- A` / `exit=1` / `cmp: /tmp/hello2.out: No such file or directory`; the implementer's own diagnosis at events.jsonl:11427: "The `cat -A` failed on macOS (BSD cat doesn't have -A) which caused the `&&` chain to break so the `python hello.py` fallback check didn't run properly".
proposed_change: In the validation paragraph (near "Only cite validation artefacts you have actually inspected"), add: "Compose verification so a failure cannot hide later evidence: run independent assertions as separate commands, or with explicit per-assertion status checks, never as one `&&` chain whose early failure suppresses the checks after it; prefer portable shell and flags (for example `od -c` rather than GNU-only `cat -A`) and confirm an unfamiliar flag works before relying on it; never report a check as passed when its command did not actually run — a missing output file or empty capture is a failed check to re-run, not a caveat."
